Cc: Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.com>
Subject: Discovery Recap: Finly — p95 latency targets, streaming UX & concurrency requirements

Hi Samir / Rachel,

Thanks again for taking the time today — great first conversation. Below is a short recap so we’re aligned on pain, success criteria, and next steps. Please reply with corrections or additions.

Call highlights / pain points
- Streaming UX is degraded: users see long delays for the first partial token and for mid-response updates (observed first-chunk ~600ms, p95 end-to-end ~1.2s).
- Concurrency bottlenecks: production load peaks ~150 concurrent interactive sessions, expected to grow to ~250 over next quarter.
- Cost + reliability tradeoffs: Finly currently runs an in-house fleet and is concerned about unit cost at scale while meeting p95 SLAs.

Current stack (as discussed)
- Model: open LLM (13B class, quantized) hosted on customer GCP A100 nodes behind a Node.js API.
- Frontend: streaming UI with per-user session affinity.
- Observed perf: p95 1.0–1.3s for short prompts, first streaming chunk ~500–700ms.

Success criteria (what Finly told us they need)
- p95 end-to-end latency <= 400ms for typical interactive requests (short prompts, <200 tokens).
- Streaming partial latency (first chunk and subsequent deltas) <= 120ms p95 to preserve smooth UX.
- Support for 200+ concurrent streaming sessions at target latency.
- No regression in output quality (accept quantization if quality stays within delta).

Proposed next steps
1) I’ll attach a short discovery slide deck and a suggested PoC/test plan (attached).
2) Looping in Aditya (SE) and Dylan (Platform) to scope performance tests and a week-long PoC.
3) Finly to share a sample traffic trace or representative prompt set and a quick infra diagram (if you’re comfortable) — we can use synthetic load if needed.
4) Propose PoC kickoff next week (any day Tue–Thu morning PT works for us).

Attachments: 20261012-finly-discovery-slide-deck.pdf (PoC plan, test config)

Thanks — talk soon,
\Marissa Cole

Subject: Re: Discovery Recap: Finly — p95 latency targets, streaming UX & concurrency requirements

Hi Samir — thanks for the details and the infra diagram. A few clarifying questions and a proposed minimal test plan so we can size resources and estimate cost: 

Clarifying questions:
- Avg tokens per interactive request? (you mentioned typical <200 tokens; a median estimate helps).
- Do you reuse KV cache / long context across turns or are most requests single-shot?
- Are sessions sticky to a particular inference instance (session affinity)?
- Model variant: exact family/weights (13B dense vs sparse, quantization format e.g., GPTQ/4-bit).
\Proposed minimal PoC test (5 days):
- Day 0: baseline capture — run existing traffic trace to confirm current p95 and streaming chunk latencies.
- Day 1–2: run controlled load tests with Redwood runtime using your prompt set: target 1) single-user latency profile; 2) concurrent test at 50/100/200 concurrent streams.
- Day 3: experiment with KV caching and prefix reuse to measure p95 improvement.
- Day 4: tuning (batching limits, kernel selection, quantization profile) to meet <=400ms p95 target for short prompts.
\Suggested test config (initial):
- Model: redwood/optim-13b-8bit (proposed quantized runtime)
- HW: 1–2 x A100 (ensuring multi-instance pool for concurrency) for each test shard; autoscaling to mimic production bursts.
- Batching: target small continuous batching window (5–10ms) for streaming-friendly latency.
- Measurement: record first-byte latency for streaming + end-to-end p95, p50, p99; token throughput; cost estimate per 1k tokens.
\Success criteria for PoC:
- p95 <= 400ms for short prompts at 200 concurrent streams OR clear mitigation plan to reach that (e.g., model variant + cache).
- Streaming first-chunk <= 120ms p95.
- Cost per 1k tokens within agreed threshold (we’ll provide numbers after initial run).
\If you can share a small representative prompt set and confirm a kickoff slot (we heard Wed 10/14 or Thu 10/15 AM PT), we’ll drop the perf harness and a basic pricing sketch ahead of the call.
\Thanks — looping Evelyn for CS/contract coordination.
\Aditya Rao
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
